held.why: REFUSED: Wrong line: 'above his company' runs across two lines ('above his' ends line 32, 'company' starts line 33), but the script says 'Line 32 says he was 'proud' and 'above his company''. Write 'Lines 32 and 33'. The land-walks precheck fails it on the same quote. The rest is true: 'till his manners gave a disgust' is on line 31, and Bingley's 'angry that the ball closed so' is on line 37.

REFUSED: Wrong line: 'Named things went in the first box to be returned.' runs across two lines ('to be' ends line 7, 'returned.' starts line 8), but the script cites 'Line 7'. Write 'Lines 7 and 8'. The precheck fails it. Also 'Yet line 33 puts it in 'the Friday box'' never shows that the Friday box is the box for things with no name going to charity (lines 8 and 9), so the child cannot see which rule is bent. Name that link.

REFUSED: 'Nothing says he adds his name.' argues from silence. A passage leaves out countless things, and this option's own tag hint tells the child to 'Find the line that proves it'. 'A place he could take and does not' then states something no line says. The script shows only that he walks past now ('passed the noticeboard', line 37). It never supports the key's future 'is not going to fill' (trials in 'September' on line 38, next to his giving away his named jumper because 'It won't fit me next year', line 47). The key is the intended reading of the writer's purpose and no other option is defensible, so the fault is in the script, not the question. Rest the step on 'passed' and on that later evidence, not on what the passage leaves out.

REFUSED: Wrong line: 'to be returned' runs across two lines ('to be' on line 7, 'returned' on line 8), but the script says 'Line 7 says ... 'to be returned''. Write 'Lines 7 and 8'. The precheck fails it. The rest is true: 'the charity collection' is on lines 8 and 9, 'had left in Year Four' is on line 13, 'anyway' is on line 14, and the step from returns-versus-charity to the key is sound.
